svg.aria-label: How to write п, и: 2 letters, п, и, one after another
svg.title: Writing п, и
svg.desc: 2 letters written one after another: п, и (cyrillic). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansCyrillic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: п: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase п demonstration, 06:26–06:31, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>; и: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase и demonstration, 03:56–04:02, YouTube, 5 February 2013 <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqDLDfYoO2o>. Source notes on variation: п: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 06:26–06:31 lowercase п demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, descends the left stem to the baseline, turns upward without lifting, rises into a rounded top shoulder, descends the right stem, and finishes through a small rising exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a rounded Latin n with entry and exit joins; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed squared arch with two straight vertical stems joined by a horizontal top bar, without the cursive joins. This learner path preserves the source's left-stem-to-top-shoulder-to-right-stem order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left stem, retrace to the upper-left junction, sweep through the top bar, and descend the right stem without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's rounded shoulder and entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the shoulder and stems differently. и: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 03:56–04:02 lowercase и demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, descends to the baseline, turns directly into a rising diagonal, descends the right stem, and finishes through a small rising exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a rounded Latin u with a rising entry side and exit join; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed backwards-N form with two straight vertical stems joined by a rising diagonal and no entry or exit joins. This learner path preserves the source's left-stem-to-rising-diagonal-to-right-stem order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left stem, turn along its baseline, rise through the diagonal, and descend the right stem without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant the stems and diagonal differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 2 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Letter 2 of 2 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase п demonstration, 06:26–06:31, YouTube, 5 February 2013
Letter 2: stroke order after RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase и demonstration, 03:56–04:02, YouTube, 5 February 2013
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
